title: Phase-1 N=21 first-attempt restart root cause (evidence)
what_happened: Audits PASS at 20:22 Asia/Shanghai. Entropy N=6,9,12,15,18 completed and were written under runs/pilot/.
N=21 entropy was admitted immediately at 20:24:16 (scheduler action=admit, in_flight=1, not a RAM-admission hold). The orchestrator then correctly entered drain and waited.
ACTIVE_STATUS/PHASE1_STATUS were only updated at wave start (20:24:16) and therefore looked stale. No N=21 result file was written because the scan writes only at the end.

The first worker (pid 2666358, parent 2664904) kept all per-field full-space ground-state vectors (2^21 complex, ~32 MiB each). RSS grew to ~4.2 GiB (ru_maxrss ~4.08e6 KiB at 20:56) with no field-level progress log.

Those processes were still running at 21:07 when they were believed gone. After identity checks (cwd=/workspace/qumode_qsk, cmdline=python3 -u scripts/run_phase1.py, lock pid=2664904), they were SIGTERM-stopped at 21:08:56 and the owned stale lock was removed.

logs/phase1_stderr.log contains BrokenProcessPool: process terminated abruptly. That traceback is from the SIGTERM of the first worker, appended to the same log, not a spontaneous runtime crash and not a CPU-policy fault.
The scan was then fixed to retain only the peak GS, reuse the previous even-sector vector as eigsh v0 (same tolerances), and log each field. Resume skipped completed audits and N<=18 entropy.

The second N=21 attempt (parent 2684987, worker 2684998) is a single nice=19 worker. Mid-scan RSS is flat at 1933780 KiB (~1.84 GiB). That is the evidence the leak, not CPU capping, was the first-attempt problem.
